text:
lee: hitting a weird case in node-sdk where fragments flip order after an auth-refresh+reconnect. repro in sample-node-app.
sami: node or browser?
lee: node 18 LTS, node-sdk v1.1.0. flow: long stream -> token refresh triggers reconnect -> stream resumes but UI reassembles wrong order.
sami: any logs?
lee: pasted server/client log snippet:
```
server: emit event id=900 seq=120 data={"stream_id":"s1","chunk_index":3}
client:onmessage lastEventId=899 event.id=900 seq=121 data={"stream_id":"s1","chunk_index":2}
client:onmessage lastEventId=901 event.id=902 seq=122 data={"stream_id":"s1","chunk_index":4}
```
so event.id increased but chunk_index goes 3 -> 2 -> 4.
toni: that suggests server may re-shard or retransmit fragments on resume. we should not assume seq==application-order.
rob: are we using resume token vs last-event-id? difference matters on auth refresh since token changes.
lee: client sends last-event-id header on reconnect. server replies with fragments but seems to re-send some older fragments.
infra-bot: scheduled maintenance 2025-01-10T03:00 UTC for edge proxy updates.
sami: immediate mitigation: node-sdk should stash fragments by (stream_id, chunk_index) and accept only the first instance, then emit in chunk_index order when contiguous. this handles duplicates and reorders.
toni: agree but be careful with memory: streams can be huge. implement sliding window and emit as we get next expected index. also time out missing indexes after Xs and emit what we have.
rob: another idea: on auth-refresh triggered reconnect, add a small jittered backoff (200-800ms) before reattaching to let the server finish re-sharding. might reduce duplicates.
lee: for now I can patch the sample-node-app to show tolerant reassembly. will file SDK PR for the stash+sliding-window behavior.
sami: add debug logging flag to surface "chunk_index decrease" and "duplicate chunk" events. helps support when customers report.
toni: tests: create a fake server that intentionally reorders on resume, run in CI matrix for node/browser SDKs.
rob: don't forget doc note in DXs "clients should defensively handle non-monotonic application chunk indexes on resume". platform will try to keep monotonic but not guaranteed during reconnection epochs.
lee: opening PRs: sample-app fix and node-sdk patch. tagging @toni @sami for reviews. thanks! :thumbsup:
